title: DevX tutorial quickfixes and sample-app gaps
content:
Morning scratchpad — focused on quick, high-impact doc fixes and sample app issues. Rough notes, to-dos, and proposed copy changes.

High-level objectives:
- Fix small doc inconsistencies that confuse users during onboarding (reduce immediate support load).
- Patch sample apps so they run locally with minimal friction (env vars, CORS, minimal deps).
- Surface a short set of examples for streaming and function/tool-calling that are identical across Node/Python/Go.

Top pain points observed (tickets + snippets):
1) Streaming example mismatch (docs vs SDK).
   - Problem: JS example shows `await client.stream()` but TS SDK uses EventEmitter style; leads to runtime error for newbies.
   - Impact: Multiple support threads in #devx-help last week.
   - Quick fix: Add both sync and event styles, mark the preferred pattern for Node 1.x.
   - TODO: Update docs PR (docs repo) with example parity. Owner: Alex. ETA: 2026-03-14.

2) Function-calling vs tools naming mismatch across languages.
   - Problem: Python tutorial calls them `tools`, Node calls `functions`; backend expects `function_call` payload.
   - Confusing line: "define tools to transform outputs" — change to "define functions (tooling)" and add glossary note.
   - Quick action: Add explicit mapping table (Python name -> Node name -> API field).
   - Linked: JIRA-INF-721.

3) Sample app `chatbot-demo` fails locally for Windows devs (CORS + missing env var).
   - Symptoms: 403 from local web server when trying to hit local proxy; README only mentions `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but sample uses `REDWOOD_KEY` in code.
   - Fixes:
     - Normalize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY in all examples.
     - Add small section "Running locally on Windows" (PowerShell examples, npx serve notes).
     - Add CORS dev proxy snippet (express) with clear warnings not to use in production.
   - PR target: examples repo PR #88. Owner: Jordan. ETA: 2026-03-15.

4) Quantization/optimize tutorial missing benchmark table.
   - Problem: We discuss q4_0, q4_k, q8_0 but don't show expected latency throughput tradeoffs or recommended hardware.
   - Proposed addition: small benchmark table (model, backend, token/sec median, memory delta) and a one-paragraph guidance: "When to pick q4_0 vs q8_0".
   - Owner: Priya. Need perf numbers from infra. Ask infra SLO: infra/perf-team slack thread.

5) Inconsistent parameter names in embeddings guide.
   - Issue: Some examples use `model: "embed-1"` others use `model_id`. Pick `model` as canonical API param across docs.
   - Quick patch: run a grep across docs repo for `model_id` and replace in examples only (leave historical notes intact).
   - Owner: Alex. ETA: 2026-03-16.

Checklist (small PRs, low-risk):
- [ ] Add matched streaming examples for Node/Python/Go (include minimal readme blurb).
- [ ] Glossary entry: tools vs functions vs function_call.
- [ ] Normalize env var names in examples (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- [ ] Add Windows local dev notes to chatbot sample README.
- [ ] Insert quantization benchmark table (placeholder values until infra measurement).
- [ ] Replace `model_id` with `model` in examples where appropriate.
- [ ] Add tests/snippets to docs CI that run sample apps with a fake key to catch env var mismatches.

Quick copy suggestions (to paste into PRs):
- Streaming section header change: "Streaming responses (Node, Python, Go) — preferred pattern and event-based fallback". Add short note: "If you need line-by-line processing, prefer the stream consumer pattern."
- Function/tools glossary: "We use the term 'functions' in the API payload (field: function_call). Example SDK param names may vary between languages; see mapping table below."

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we want to standardize on `REDWOOD_API_KEY` across all repos? (Yes — talk to infra about secret scanning to update existing demos.)
- Can infra run quick quant benchmarks on `r-instruct-7b` q4_0 vs q8_0 on an A10G? I need median latency and token/sec for 512 token sequences. (Ping: @infra-perf)
- Are there any legal/compliance examples we should exclude from public sample apps? (Ask Legal if we're including synthetic PII in examples.)

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Draft PRs this afternoon: streaming parity + env var normalizations. Link templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/compare/tutorial-streaming.
- Add small CI job that runs `node examples/chatbot-demo` with `REDWOOD_API_KEY=local_test` to detect early failure; keep it optional (allow fail) until fixes land.
- Put small blurb in release notes for minor doc sync: "Normalized environment variables and fixed streaming examples" — include links to PRs.

Rough time box: 6 hours today for Alex to open initial PRs. Coordinate with Jordan on examples PR to avoid merge conflicts.

End of scratchpad.

(If I don't get to these tonight, move streaming examples to next sprint as top priority.)
